# External test-selection evaluation

Can CodeAtlas's test selection be trusted to leave tests out on external
Rust projects? Measured on four repositories under the protocol in
[PROTOCOL.md](PROTOCOL.md), which was committed (with its pinned inputs)
before any probe ran on them. Deviations made since are listed there.

**Short answer: no.** Over 107 probes in which some test executed the
probed function, CodeAtlas's resolved-call selection found 7.6% of the
failing tests (whole suite) and missed none in only 3 probes. Including
ambiguous calls raises that to 23.8% and 18 probes. Most misses (2,349 of
2,936) are tests generated by macros, which the analysis cannot see. The
conservative check added for this reason recommended the full suite for
all 160 probes; each time at least one blind spot applied.

## Inputs

| Repository | Commit | Why chosen | Tests | Invisible | Packages | Build / run (s) |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ripgrep | `3fce3b5` | macro-generated integration tests that run the `rg` binary | 1,206 | 722 | 11 | 8.5 / 1.9 |
| serde_json | `20572a6` (v1.0.154) | items from `macro_rules!`, generic `Serializer` / `Deserializer` dispatch | 143 | 8 | 1 | 7.2 / 0.2 |
| itertools | `37bd72a` (v0.15.0) | generic adapters, quickcheck-generated tests | 444 | 298 | 1 | 11.3 / 5.5 |
| bytes | `76c0fbb` (v1.12.1) | cfg-gated variants, `Buf` / `BufMut` trait generics | 1,055 | 873 | 1 | 2.3 / 0.8 |

*Tests*: default features, passing in both baseline runs (no flaky tests
were found). *Invisible*: tests with no symbol in the analysis: generated
by `rgtest!`, `quickcheck!` or bytes's `buf_tests!`, or in modules that
serde_json declares with `automod::dir!`. *Build /
run*: one baseline build of the test binaries and one run of all of them,
inside the container. Toolchain: rustc 1.99.1 in
`rust:1.99-slim-bookworm@sha256:f2c004e3…`. 40 functions per repository
(seed 11), all 160 probes built and completed; 53 probed functions were
executed by no test.

## Results

Whole-suite recall: failing tests selected over all failing tests,
micro-averaged. *Safe*: probes (with at least one failing test) in which
no failing test was missed. *Time saved*: 1 − summed libtest times of the
selected tests over those of the whole suite, mean per probe; building is
not included and is the same for every strategy except `changed-package`,
which could skip building other packages (not measured).

| Strategy | Recall | Safe | Missed invisible | Missed visible |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| run-all | 1.000 | 107/107 | 0 | 0 |
| changed-package | 1.000 | 107/107 | 0 | 0 |
| file-dependency | 0.255 | 32/107 | 2,349 | 20 |
| name-mention | 0.512 | 43/107 | 1,334 | 218 |
| codeatlas | 0.076 | 3/107 | 2,349 | 587 |
| codeatlas-ambiguous | 0.238 | 18/107 | 2,349 | 74 |
| codeatlas-conservative | 1.000 | 107/107 | 0 | 0 |

`run-all` and `codeatlas-conservative` select every test in every probe
(recall 1, time saved 0) and are left out of this table. All rows, with
`share` and missed counts, are in [results/](results/); the
[analysis script](analyze.py) prints them.

Secondary, with a different denominator: recall over *visible* failing
tests only (those with a symbol) is 0.268 / 0.449 / 0.064 / 0.354 for
`codeatlas` and 0.996 / 0.813 / 0.679 / 0.859 for `codeatlas-ambiguous`
(ripgrep / serde_json / itertools / bytes). It says how well the graph
covers what it can see; it says nothing about whether selected tests can
replace the suite.

## Failure analysis

Of the 3,178 failing tests over all probes, `codeatlas` missed 2,936:

| Cause | Missed | How identified |
|---|---:|---|
| Invisible tests (generated by macros) | 2,349 | test has no symbol; all of them were missed by every analysis-based strategy |
| Visible, found once ambiguous calls are followed | 513 | selected by `codeatlas-ambiguous` |
| Visible, missed even with ambiguous calls | 74 | listed below |

* **Invisible tests dominate.** ripgrep's `rgtest!` integration tests
  (1,490 missed failures) and `globset` tests (13); itertools' quickcheck
  properties (`quick` 104, `specializations` 41, `test_std` 16,
  `laziness` 11); bytes' `buf_tests!` module in `tests/test_buf.rs` (667);
  serde_json's `regression` tests (7), whose modules come from
  `automod::dir!`. Without expanding `macro_rules!`
  and procedural test macros these cannot be selected. The ripgrep
  integration tests also run the `rg` binary as a separate process.
* **Visible misses are mostly ambiguous dispatch.** 513 of the 587 are
  found when ambiguous calls are followed: calls through generic
  parameters (`Matcher`, `Sink`, `Buf`) and method calls whose receiver
  type is not inferred. Following them costs precision (selected share
  rises from 0.4% to 5.1% on average).
* **The remaining 74** (32 probes, listed by `analyze.py`) are reached
  through calls the graph classifies as external or never records. In 22
  of the 32 probes the probed method implements a trait from outside the
  repository (`Iterator::next`, `PartialEq::eq`, `io::Read::read`, serde's
  `Serializer` and `Deserializer`), so its callers are in the standard
  library or serde. Extension-trait methods called on standard-library
  values are classified as external calls: in itertools,
  `mix_data().flatten_ok()` on a `vec::IntoIter` has no edge, although
  `Itertools` is implemented for every iterator. And bytes stores
  `promotable_even_clone` in a vtable of function pointers.
* **Not a CodeAtlas limitation but a probe one:** one bytes run recorded
  no probes because CodeAtlas dropped the library target when a bench
  target had the same name. Fixed before `bytes` was probed again
  (deviation 5).

## The conservative check

`codeatlas-conservative` falls back to the full suite whenever the check
in [docs/impact-analysis.md](../../docs/impact-analysis.md#when-selective-execution-is-unsafe)
finds a blind spot. Reasons fired (probes out of 40):

| Repository | Test macros | Ambiguous callers | Hidden mentions | External trait | Unresolved calls |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ripgrep | 40 | 25 | 19 | 7 | 0 |
| serde_json | 40 | 19 | 7 | 27 | 3 |
| itertools | 40 | 32 | 33 | 17 | 0 |
| bytes | 40 | 24 | 25 | 21 | 5 |

It allowed selective execution in 0 of 160 probes, so it never accepted
an incomplete selection, and never saved anything. Every repository has
item-level macros in its test code, and in all four some of them do
generate tests. Without that reason (a post-hoc check, not part of the
rule), 11 probes would have been allowed; 5 of them were executed by
tests, and 2 of those 5 missed failing tests (247, all invisible). The
other reasons alone flagged every probe with a visible miss. On these
repositories the check's honest answer is "run the full suite", and it is
a heuristic: a probe it allows is not proven safe.

## What would help, measured against this

* **Package-level selection is the only reliable saving here.**
  `changed-package` found every failing test in all 107 probes and saved
  27.9% of test time on ripgrep, the one multi-package workspace; on
  single-package repositories it is the full suite. Cargo's dependency
  graph bounds which code a test can link (process spawning and data
  files aside), which the call graph does not.
* **Seeing macro-generated tests** is the largest gap: 80% of the
  missed failing tests, which no analysis-based strategy here selected.
* Better receiver-type inference would turn ambiguous candidates into
  resolved calls and so recover precision. For recall, following the
  ambiguous calls shows the reach of that: 513 of the 587 visible misses.

## Reproducing

Requires Docker and about 3 GB of disk. `setup` needs the network (image,
clones at the pinned commits, dependency downloads, building CodeAtlas in
the container); probes run with `--network none` on a read-only mount of
the clone and build in a scratch copy inside the container.

```bash
benchmarks/external/run.sh setup
```

```bash
for r in ripgrep serde_json itertools bytes; do benchmarks/external/run.sh probe $r primary; done
```

```bash
for r in ripgrep serde_json itertools bytes; do benchmarks/external/run.sh compare $r primary; done
```

```bash
python3 benchmarks/external/analyze.py primary
```

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `PROTOCOL.md` | Frozen protocol and deviations |
| `repos.json` | Pinned commits, image digest, probe seeds |
| `locks/` | Lockfiles generated once for the libraries without one |
| `raw/*-truth.json` | Ground truth: tests, flaky tests, per-test times, packages, every probe's failing tests and timings |
| `results/*-comparison.json` | Every strategy per probe: selected, true positives, missed tests (visible by ID, invisible by count), time share; reasons the check gave |

Each probe took 0–8 s here (incremental rebuild plus one suite run);
the four primary sets took about 10 minutes in total on an Apple Silicon
Mac. The held-out seed (12) was not run: no change to selection was made
in response to these results.
